# Test fixtures

| File | Source | License |
|---|---|---|
| `disk-af.img`, `testfs1-af` | Generated by `scripts/make_af_fixture.py` from `testfs1` | as `testfs1` |
| `disk-af.E01`, `disk-af-split.E01`..`.E03`, `disk-af-odd.E01` | Generated by `scripts/make_e01_fixture.py` from `disk-af.img`; test images, not evidence | as `testfs1` |
| `disk-win.img`, `testfs1-win` | Generated by `scripts/make_win_fixture.py` from `testfs1-af`: synthetic Windows artifacts (hives, event logs, Prefetch, LNK, Jump Lists) at their real paths, plus carving ground truth from `scripts/fixture_carve.py` (files in free clusters, a deleted picture whose clusters are free, samples, lookalikes and a cut-off JPEG in a 2 MiB unpartitioned tail). Invented data: LAB-PC, documentation IP ranges, `.test` domains | as `testfs1` |
| `win/` | Generated by `scripts/fixture_windows.py`: the same artifacts as single files, plus LZXPRESS Huffman vectors produced by Windows' own `RtlCompressBuffer` | as `testfs1` |
| `fat12.img`, `fat16.img`, `fat32.img`, `exfat.img`, `disk-fat.img` | Generated by `scripts/make_fat_fixture.py` (pure Python, no mkfs needed): the same small story on each file system (a fragmented long-named file, a deleted file with free clusters, a deleted file whose clusters were reused, a deleted folder) and an MBR disk with the FAT32 and exFAT volumes as two partitions. The FAT32 volume has fewer clusters than Microsoft's FAT32 minimum to stay small; Kokino and Linux go by its layout, Windows would not mount it | Invented data |
| `photo/` | Generated by `scripts/make_photo_fixture.py` (Pillow, numpy): a synthetic "camera" photo with custom tables, EXIF, GPS and thumbnail, and variants with known findings (edited with the old thumbnail kept, re-saved with libjpeg tables, cropped, double-compressed, ZIP appended, cloned region, PNG and BMP with LSB-embedded data in the first 30%) | Invented data |
| `testfs1` | 2 MiB NTFS volume from the `ntfs` crate by Colin Finck (`testdata/testfs1`, built with mkntfs, see `create-testfs1.sh` in that crate) | MIT OR Apache-2.0 |
